build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

exclude: not picture 49: its packed bytes end on the disk where picture 50's packed bytes begin, and the unpacker reads on to the end of its 4-sector window, so these are those bytes decoded with picture 49's value table (side 2's, this snapshot's). Nothing reads them

comments.text: Picture 49's header, read by start_picture ($0586): its area, columns 1 to 11 and pixel rows 16 to 99 (inside the picture window, which picture_window_open $12CF clears from pixel row 16 to 111); then five words counted from the picture's start ($CA00, where load_portrait $2631 unpacks it): the base frame at +$004E, channel 0's script at +$000E, channel 1's script at +$001B, channel 2's script at +$0034 and channel 3's script at +$003E.

Channel 0's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 4 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 1 then 1, frame 2 then 2, frame 2 then 1, frame 1 then 2. One pass takes 6 steps.

Channel 1's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 8 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 5, frame 4 then 25, frame 5 then 2, frame 5 then 15, frame 5 then 2, frame 6 then 10, frame 4 then 30, frame 4 then 10. One pass takes 99 steps.

Channel 2's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 3 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 5, frame 7 then 40, frame 7 then 10. One pass takes 55 steps.

Channel 3's script, read by animate_picture_tick ($05F4-$0646): 5 entries of a delay byte and a frame word counted from the picture's start, then the $FF that sends the channel back to its first entry. Each entry XORs its frame onto the picture, then the channel waits that many steps: frame 3 then 1, frame 8 then 1, frame 9 then 8, frame 9 then 1, frame 8 then 1. One pass takes 12 steps.

Picture 49's base frame, which start_picture draws by storing (draw_frame_store $064E): a run count of 0 to start, then one block from column 1, pixel row 16, with $02 as its escape byte. Its bytes go down each column and on to the top of the next until the area is full: 924 bitmap bytes, written with 30 runs (the escape byte, then a count and a value).

Frame 1 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 1 and 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 2 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 0's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 14 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 5 to 6. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 3 of picture 49, named by channel 1's entry 1, channel 2's entry 1 and channel 3's entry 1: empty, a run count of 0 and the $FF that ends the frame, so draw_frame_xor ($0648) changes nothing and the entry only waits.

Frame 4 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 2, 7 and 8: a run count of 0 to start, then 6 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 21 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 5 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entries 3, 4 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 12 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 6 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 1's entry 6: a run count of 0 to start, then 4 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 30 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 4 to 7. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 7 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 2's entries 2 and 3: a run count of 0 to start, then 5 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 29 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 3 to 8. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 8 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 3's entries 2 and 5: a run count of 0 to start, then 3 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 29 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 8 to 10. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.

Frame 9 of picture 49, XORed onto the picture (draw_frame_xor $0648) by channel 3's entries 3 and 4: a run count of 0 to start, then 2 blocks of a column, a pixel row and an escape byte, 13 bitmap bytes in all, in columns 8 to 9. A $00 ends a block, and a column byte of $FF ends the frame.
The last byte picture 49's own packed bytes decode to, the 982nd byte from $CA00: the unpacker makes it from the bits left over in the stream's last byte. Nothing reads it.
